clue.text: Means to communicate in period without company

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the period word goes around the company abbreviation

parts.note: a term is a period of time, as in a school term

explanation.surface: Someone describes a way of keeping in touch during a stretch of time with no firm involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal telephone or speaker system, a device for talking between rooms.

clue.text: Architects presented with line drawing originally blue

parts.note: RIBA is the Royal Institute of British Architects

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word drawing

explanation.surface: Architects are handed a line drawing that was first done in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour in the drawing; it means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are indecent ones, and ribald humour is coarse and vulgar in the same way.

clue.text: Like to see cracking wrestling from the bottom team

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the letter for see goes inside the wrestling word
in a down clue, read from the bottom means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: all-in is a free-style form of wrestling
V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A fan of wrestling confesses an urge to watch the lowest-placed side get a hammering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the bottom' reverses ALLIN to NILLA; 'cracking' puts V inside it after the N. 'from the bottom team' teases a relegation struggle. ASTON VILLA is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English football club, so it is one example of a sports side.

clue.text: British monarch keeps bird in hat

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the bird sits inside the abbreviations for British and monarch

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A British king or queen holds a bird inside a hat, a conjuring trick at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard round felt hat with a narrow brim, worn by City gents.

clue.text: Artist took the stage, being filmed

parts.note: on came, as in 'on came the clowns', means made an entrance onto the stage
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter stepped out onto the boards while the cameras were rolling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the entry as a stage direction, on came RA: the artist made an entrance, though the clue names the artist first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on camera is in shot, captured by the lens as it is recorded.

clue.text: One having party back in holiday island

indicators.note: back says the letters for one and the party are read in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Lab is short for Labour, a political party; having joins it on

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party on returning to a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses I and LAB together; Labour is a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island famous as a tourist destination for beach holidays.

clue.text: Old man making climb with little desire

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the old man's letters run backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man
petite means small or little

explanation.surface: An elderly father tackles a climb without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making climb' turns PA upwards into AP.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving or a wish for something, not only food.

clue.text: Problem ship coming into sound

indicators.note: coming into says the ship letters enter the middle of the healthy word

parts.note: sound here means healthy, as hale does
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel sailing into a strait runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a stretch of water, which suits the ship; it means healthy, HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a bother or difficulty, a nuisance that has to be dealt with.

clue.text: Finally settles trouble between North and South Irish region

indicators.note: between places the trouble word inside, flanked by the North and South letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A dispute between North and South over an Irish region is at last resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' belongs to the definition, not a last-letter signal. County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something down is to fix it firmly or make it definite, a phrasal verb for securing agreement.

clue.text: Dominant mountain has to be truncated

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the word has loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A towering peak must be lopped off at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be truncated' drops the final S of HAS, giving HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha as an adjective describes the top-ranking member of a group, as in an alpha male.

clue.text: Time and time again, love is an inspiration

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
time a second time, abbreviated to T
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Love, again and again, is a source of creative spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and a Muse is a goddess of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Green state imposed penalty probing corrupt sales

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so the penalty word goes inside the jumbled letters
corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters of sales are rearranged

parts.note: to fine is to impose a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded government fines dishonest trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests environmental politics; here it means leafy and verdant.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafiness is the condition of being full of foliage, so verdant growth makes a green condition.

clue.text: Corpse found in vehicle crossing channel

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning, so the vehicle stretches around the channel name

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Dave is a British TV channel

explanation.surface: A body turns up in a car on a cross-Channel ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests the English Channel; it is Dave, a UK television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, especially one used for medical study.

clue.text: Connected, make certain to install it for Romeo

indicators.note: to install it for the letter means put it in place of that letter

parts.note: ensure means make certain
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A technician double-checks an installation done for someone called Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to install it for Romeo' swaps the R in ENSURE for IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite room is joined directly to a bedroom, so it is attached rather than separate.

clue.text: Nastiness with a drunken composer

indicators.note: drunken means reeling and disordered, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A musician's unpleasantness is fuelled by drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges NASTINESS plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saëns was a French Romantic who wrote The Carnival of the Animals.

clue.text: Some extreme talent needed in heavy music

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Heavy rock bands call for a few prodigious players.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'needed in heavy music' as the definition, but 'needed in' only links; heavy music alone defines the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal, or heavy metal, is a loud, guitar-driven rock genre.

clue.text: Idiot, accepting direction, to have linked community

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the direction letter goes inside the idiot word

parts.note: a twit is a fool
N, for north, is a compass direction
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: A fool takes instructions so as to belong to a connected group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' looks like an instruction but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin town is one formally paired with a town abroad for cultural exchange.

clue.text: Climber in training area

parts.note: PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: A mountaineer works out in the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is the climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a climbing plant, gripping supports with tendrils.

clue.text: Machiavellian character pens ordinary verse for pigeon

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the ordinary and verse letters go inside the character

parts.note: Machiavelli's best-known work is The Prince
O is short for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A scheming figure writes plain lines of poetry about a pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing; it means encloses. 'Not my pigeon' is a British idiom for not my business.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon, in 'not my pigeon', means one's concern or area of responsibility, as does province.

clue.text: Current understanding serves as example

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a deal is an agreement or understanding

explanation.surface: The present agreement is held up as a model for others.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection, a model to follow.

clue.text: Coil on sink offers security measure

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the coil word comes first

parts.note: a lock is a coil or curl of hair
to sink a drink is to down it

explanation.surface: A plumber offers a coil of pipe on a kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a basin; it means swallow, DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lockdown confines people in place, a restriction imposed for safety.

clue.text: Lake Michigan port appealingly elegant in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish and attractive
ago means in the past, as in years ago

explanation.surface: A lakeside city once had real style.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago, Illinois, lies on Lake Michigan's south-western shore and is a major Great Lakes harbour.

clue.text: Man from Lima in class

indicators.note: in puts the Lima letter inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Peruvian man finds himself in a classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, not a person; 'Lima' is a NATO letter, not Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and the castle, or rook, is one of them.

clue.text: A saint out and about like his adversary

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of a saint are rearranged

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A holy man goes out and about acting like his enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out and about' looks like one phrase; 'out' rearranges A SAINT, 'about' is C.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the arch-enemy of the holy, so what resembles a saint's foe is devilish.

clue.text: Secretary follows small female mountain guide

indicators.note: follows says the secretary letters come after the other two pieces

parts.note: her is a female pronoun
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary trails a small woman who leads climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famed as climbing guides and porters on Everest.

clue.text: In buff, nether regions one displays?

definitions.text: In buff, nether regions one displays?

indicators.note: In tells us the underworld word sits inside the enthusiast word

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, as is a nut, as in film buff
Dis is the underworld, Dante's city of Hell

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about who bares their bottom when in the buff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buff' looks like naked but means an enthusiast; 'In' is the container signal. The whole clue also describes a naturist.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed by choice, so their private parts are on view.

clue.text: Light, refreshing tins of beer unopened

indicators.note: refreshing means renewing, so the letters are made over in a new order
unopened means without its first letter, so beer loses its B

explanation.surface: A light, refreshing drink comes from cans of ale not yet cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' cuts BEER to EER; 'refreshing' rearranges TINSOF plus EER.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire is to ignite it, to make something burn.

clue.text: Ham producer allows seconds in for a feed

indicators.note: in for a means the seconds letter goes in place of the letter a

parts.note: Noah was the father of Ham in the Bible

explanation.surface: A pig farmer allows second helpings at feeding time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham producer' suggests a pig farmer; it is NOAH, father of Ham. 'allows seconds in for a' swaps his A for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food or a meal, and to have a feed means to eat.

clue.text: Extra Norse works returned by daughter

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the Norse works are read in reverse

parts.note: the Eddas are collections of Old Norse poetry

explanation.surface: A daughter sends back old Scandinavian books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns EDDA into ADDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Added as an adjective means additional, put on top.

clue.text: Western isle stormy?

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Is the Hebridean island battered by gales?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges W and ISLE. Lewis is in the Outer Hebrides, the Western Isles of Scotland, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is the northern part of Lewis and Harris, the largest island of the Western Isles.

clue.text: Understood after holding one's own tool

indicators.note: after says the understood word comes behind the holding word

parts.note: coping means managing, holding one's own
saw means understood, as in I saw what she meant

explanation.surface: Someone got the point after managing with their own kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a fine-bladed hand saw for cutting curves in wood.
